Is Planar Defines the effector as either a single dimension object i.e. a plane or the mesh is Non-manifold . This ensures that the fluid simulator will give the most accurate results for these types of meshes. Surface Emission Maximum distance in Voxels from the surface of the mesh in which fluid is emitted. Volume Emission Fire or Smoke Only : Amount of fluid to emit inside the emitter mesh, where 0 is none and 1 is the full amount. This document is intended to familiarize you with Blender Python API but not to fully cover each topic. A quick list of helpful things to know before starting: Enable Developer Extra and Python Tooltips . The Python Console is great for testing one-liners; it has autocompletion so you can inspect the API quickly. Button tooltips show Python attributes and operator names (when enabled see above). The context menu of buttons directly links to this API documentation (when enabled see above). Many python examples can be found in the text editor’s template menu. To examine further scripts distributed with Blender, see: scripts/startup/bl_ui for the user interface. scripts/startup/bl_operators for operators. Exact location depends on platform, see: directory layout docs . Running Scripts The two most common ways to execute Python scripts are using the built-in text editor or entering commands in the Python console. Both the Text Editor and Python Console are space types you can select from the header. Rather than manually configuring your spaces for Python development, you can use the Scripting workspace accessible from the Topbar tabs. From the text editor you can open .py files or paste them from the clipboard, then test using Run Script . The Python Console is typically used for typing in snippets and for testing to get immediate feedback, but can also have entire scripts pasted into it. Next see the execute function, which takes an instance of the operator and the current context. A common prefix is not used for functions. Blender has an embedded Python interpreter which is loaded when Blender is started and stays active while Blender is running. This interpreter runs scripts to draw the user interface and is used for some of Blender’s internal tools as well. Blender’s embedded interpreter provides a typical Python environment, so code from tutorials on how to write Python scripts can also be run with Blender’s interpreter. Blender provides its Python modules, such as bpy and mathutils , to the embedded interpreter so they can be imported into a script and give access to Blender’s data, classes, and functions. Scripts that deal with Blender data will need to import the modules to work. When calling an operator you may want to pass the execution context. This determines the context that is given for the operator to run in, and whether invoke() is called or only execute(). Provides Python access to calling operators, this includes operators written in C++, Python or macros. Only keyword arguments can be used to pass operator properties. Operators don’t have return values as you might expect, instead they return a set() which is made up of: {'RUNNING_MODAL', 'CANCELLED', 'FINISHED', 'PASS_THROUGH'} . Common return values are {'FINISHED'} and {'CANCELLED'} , the latter meaning that the operator execution was aborted without making any changes or saving an undo history entry. If operator was cancelled but there wasn’t any reports from it with {'ERROR'} type, it will just return {'CANCELLED'} without raising any exceptions. However, if there are error reports, a RuntimeError will be raised after the operator finishes execution, including all error report messages, regardless of the return status (even if it was {'FINISHED'} ). Provides Python access to calling operators, this includes operators written in C++, Python or macros. Only keyword arguments can be used to pass operator properties. Operators don’t have return values as you might expect, instead they return a set() which is made up of: {'RUNNING_MODAL', 'CANCELLED', 'FINISHED', 'PASS_THROUGH'} . Common return values are {'FINISHED'} and {'CANCELLED'} , the latter meaning that the operator execution was aborted without making any changes or saving an undo history entry. If operator was cancelled but there wasn’t any reports from it with {'ERROR'} type, it will just return {'CANCELLED'} without raising any exceptions. However, if there are error reports, a RuntimeError will be raised after the operator finishes execution, including all error report messages, regardless of the return status (even if it was {'FINISHED'} ). Calling an operator in the wrong context will raise a RuntimeError , there is a poll() method to avoid this problem. {"code":"import bpy
import os
import math
from mathutils import Vector

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# shakedown_fire_2iter - Mantaflow Fire (Replay Cache)
# Blender: 5.0
# Notes:
# - This script avoids unverified fluid baking operators.
# - It uses DOMAIN cache_type='REPLAY' so the simulation evaluates on-demand.
# - Only the VERIFIED dset.* / fset.* attributes from the provided APISpec
#   are assigned in this script.
# ------------------------------------------------------------

ASSET_NAME = "shakedown_fire_2iter"
FRAME_START = 1
FRAME_END = 10
DOMAIN_RESOLUTION = 32

# Relative to the .blend file (or current working directory if unsaved)
CACHE_DIR = f"//cache_{ASSET_NAME}"
RENDER_DIR = f"//renders_{ASSET_NAME}"


def ensure_dir(blender_path: str):
    """Create directory for Blender // relative paths."""
    abs_path = bpy.path.abspath(blender_path)
    os.makedirs(abs_path, exist_ok=True)
    return abs_path


def clear_scene():
    bpy.ops.object.select_all(action='SELECT')
    bpy.ops.object.delete(use_global=False)

    # Purge orphan data blocks (safe for iterative runs)
    try:
        # Blender 5+ supports recursive orphan purge via outliner operator,
        # but context may fail in background. Use data-block unlink approach.
        pass
    except Exception:
        pass

    for datablock in (
        bpy.data.meshes,
        bpy.data.materials,
        bpy.data.lights,
        bpy.data.cameras,
        bpy.data.images,
        bpy.data.textures,
    ):
        for block in list(datablock):
            if block.users == 0:
                datablock.remove(block)


def set_scene_basics():
    scene = bpy.context.scene
    scene.frame_start = FRAME_START
    scene.frame_end = FRAME_END

    # Render setup
    scene.render.engine = 'CYCLES'
    scene.cycles.samples = 96
    scene.cycles.preview_samples = 32

    scene.render.resolution_x = 1280
    scene.render.resolution_y = 720
    scene.render.resolution_percentage = 100

    scene.render.film_transparent = False

    # Color management (Filmic is default; keep explicit for repeatability)
    try:
        scene.view_settings.view_transform = 'Filmic'
        scene.view_settings.look = 'Medium High Contrast'
        scene.view_settings.exposure = 0.0
        scene.view_settings.gamma = 1.0
    except Exception:
        pass

    # Output
    ensure_dir(RENDER_DIR)
    scene.render.image_settings.file_format = 'PNG'
    scene.render.image_settings.color_mode = 'RGBA'


def look_at(obj, target: Vector):
    """Rotate obj so its -Z axis points at target."""
    direction = (target - obj.location).normalized()
    # Blender cameras look down -Z, with Y up.
    rot_quat = direction.to_track_quat('-Z', 'Y')
    obj.rotation_euler = rot_quat.to_euler()


def create_world():
    world = bpy.data.worlds.new("World_Fire")
    bpy.context.scene.world = world
    world.use_nodes = True
    nt = world.node_tree
    nodes = nt.nodes
    links = nt.links
    nodes.clear()

    n_out = nodes.new('ShaderNodeOutputWorld')
    n_bg = nodes.new('ShaderNodeBackground')
    n_bg.inputs['Color'].default_value = (0.02, 0.02, 0.025, 1.0)
    n_bg.inputs['Strength'].default_value = 0.35

    links.new(n_bg.outputs['Background'], n_out.inputs['Surface'])


def make_ground_material():
    mat = bpy.data.materials.new("MAT_Ground")
    mat.use_nodes = True
    nt = mat.node_tree
    nodes = nt.nodes
    links = nt.links
    nodes.clear()

    out = nodes.new('ShaderNodeOutputMaterial')
    bsdf = nodes.new('ShaderNodeBsdfPrincipled')

    bsdf.inputs['Base Color'].default_value = (0.06, 0.05, 0.045, 1.0)
    bsdf.inputs['Roughness'].default_value = 0.95
    bsdf.inputs['Specular IOR Level'].default_value = 0.1

    links.new(bsdf.outputs['BSDF'], out.inputs['Surface'])
    return mat


def make_log_material():
    mat = bpy.data.materials.new("MAT_Log")
    mat.use_nodes = True
    nt = mat.node_tree
    nodes = nt.nodes
    links = nt.links
    nodes.clear()

    out = nodes.new('ShaderNodeOutputMaterial')
    bsdf = nodes.new('ShaderNodeBsdfPrincipled')

    bsdf.inputs['Base Color'].default_value = (0.07, 0.04, 0.02, 1.0)
    bsdf.inputs['Roughness'].default_value = 0.9
    bsdf.inputs['Specular IOR Level'].default_value = 0.15

    # Slight emission to simulate glowing embers on logs (very subtle)
    bsdf.inputs['Emission Color'].default_value = (1.0, 0.4, 0.12, 1.0)
    bsdf.inputs['Emission Strength'].default_value = 0.05

    links.new(bsdf.outputs['BSDF'], out.inputs['Surface'])
    return mat


def make_fire_volume_material():
    """A domain volume shader driven by Mantaflow grids (flame/density).

    This is a robust starting point:
    - Attribute('flame') drives emission strength and a color ramp.
    - Attribute('density') drives volume density for smoke/attenuation.

    If a specific grid name differs, Blender will default that attribute to 0.
    """
    mat = bpy.data.materials.new("MAT_FireVolume")
    mat.use_nodes = True

    nt = mat.node_tree
    nodes = nt.nodes
    links = nt.links
    nodes.clear()

    out = nodes.new('ShaderNodeOutputMaterial')

    # Principled Volume is a convenient one-node volume model.
    vol = nodes.new('ShaderNodeVolumePrincipled')
    vol.location = (500, 0)

    # Read grids (Mantaflow typically provides 'density' and 'flame')
    attr_density = nodes.new('ShaderNodeAttribute')
    attr_density.attribute_name = 'density'
    attr_density.location = (-700, -160)

    attr_flame = nodes.new('ShaderNodeAttribute')
    attr_flame.attribute_name = 'flame'
    attr_flame.location = (-700, 140)

    # Shape the flame signal
    flame_ramp = nodes.new('ShaderNodeValToRGB')
    flame_ramp.location = (-250, 220)
    # dark -> red/orange -> yellow/white
    ramp = flame_ramp.color_ramp
    ramp.elements[0].position = 0.0
    ramp.elements[0].color = (0.0, 0.0, 0.0, 1.0)
    e1 = ramp.elements.new(0.25)
    e1.color = (0.8, 0.08, 0.01, 1.0)
    e2 = ramp.elements.new(0.55)
    e2.color = (1.0, 0.45, 0.05, 1.0)
    ramp.elements[1].position = 1.0
    ramp.elements[1].color = (1.0, 0.95, 0.7, 1.0)

    flame_gain = nodes.new('ShaderNodeMath')
    flame_gain.operation = 'MULTIPLY'
    flame_gain.inputs[1].default_value = 35.0
    flame_gain.location = (-240, 60)

    # Density shaping
    density_gain = nodes.new('ShaderNodeMath')
    density_gain.operation = 'MULTIPLY'
    density_gain.inputs[1].default_value = 2.5
    density_gain.location = (-240, -160)

    # Hook up:
    links.new(attr_flame.outputs['Fac'], flame_ramp.inputs['Fac'])
    links.new(attr_flame.outputs['Fac'], flame_gain.inputs[0])

    links.new(attr_density.outputs['Fac'], density_gain.inputs[0])

    # Principled Volume inputs
    # - Density: controls extinction.
    # - Emission Strength: drives brightness.
    # - Emission Color: drives flame color.
    links.new(density_gain.outputs['Value'], vol.inputs['Density'])
    links.new(flame_gain.outputs['Value'], vol.inputs['Emission Strength'])
    links.new(flame_ramp.outputs['Color'], vol.inputs['Emission Color'])

    # Slightly warm blackbody-ish base
    vol.inputs['Color'].default_value = (0.55, 0.55, 0.55, 1.0)
    vol.inputs['Anisotropy'].default_value = 0.1

    links.new(vol.outputs['Volume'], out.inputs['Volume'])

    # No surface for domain (pure volume)
    return mat


def create_environment_geometry(ground_mat, log_mat):
    # Ground plane
    bpy.ops.mesh.primitive_plane_add(size=10.0, location=(0.0, 0.0, 0.0))
    ground = bpy.context.active_object
    ground.name = "Ground"
    ground.data.materials.append(ground_mat)

    # Add a subtle displacement-ish look using simple geometry (no modifiers needed)
    bpy.ops.object.shade_smooth()

    # Campfire logs: 3 cylinders arranged around the center
    logs = []
    for i in range(3):
        angle = i * (2.0 * math.pi / 3.0) + 0.2
        x = math.cos(angle) * 0.25
        y = math.sin(angle) * 0.25

        bpy.ops.mesh.primitive_cylinder_add(
            vertices=24,
            radius=0.05,
            depth=0.7,
            location=(x, y, 0.05),
        )
        log = bpy.context.active_object
        log.name = f"Log_{i+1:02d}"
        log.rotation_euler = (math.radians(80), 0.0, angle + math.radians(90))
        log.data.materials.append(log_mat)
        bpy.ops.object.shade_smooth()
        logs.append(log)

    # Small stone ring (optional)
    for i in range(10):
        angle = i * (2.0 * math.pi / 10.0)
        r = 0.38 + (0.02 if i % 2 == 0 else 0.0)
        x = math.cos(angle) * r
        y = math.sin(angle) * r
        bpy.ops.mesh.primitive_ico_sphere_add(subdivisions=1, radius=0.04, location=(x, y, 0.04))
        stone = bpy.context.active_object
        stone.name = f"Stone_{i+1:02d}"
        stone.rotation_euler = (0.0, 0.0, angle)
        bpy.ops.object.shade_smooth()

        # Simple stone material per-object using a shared material
        if "MAT_Stone" not in bpy.data.materials:
            smat = bpy.data.materials.new("MAT_Stone")
            smat.use_nodes = True
            nt = smat.node_tree
            nodes = nt.nodes
            links = nt.links
            nodes.clear()
            out = nodes.new('ShaderNodeOutputMaterial')
            bsdf = nodes.new('ShaderNodeBsdfPrincipled')
            bsdf.inputs['Base Color'].default_value = (0.12, 0.12, 0.13, 1.0)
            bsdf.inputs['Roughness'].default_value = 0.98
            bsdf.inputs['Specular IOR Level'].default_value = 0.05
            links.new(bsdf.outputs['BSDF'], out.inputs['Surface'])
        stone.data.materials.append(bpy.data.materials["MAT_Stone"])


def create_flow_emitter():
    """Create a small emitter at the center of the fire."""
    bpy.ops.mesh.primitive_uv_sphere_add(radius=0.06, location=(0.0, 0.0, 0.06))
    emitter = bpy.context.active_object
    emitter.name = "Fire_Emitter"

    # Slightly elongate vertically to form a base of the flame
    emitter.scale = (1.0, 1.0, 0.65)
    bpy.ops.object.transform_apply(location=False, rotation=False, scale=True)

    return emitter


def create_domain_cube(volume_mat):
    """Create a Mantaflow gas domain cube."""
    bpy.ops.mesh.primitive_cube_add(size=2.0, location=(0.0, 0.0, 1.0))
    domain = bpy.context.active_object
    domain.name = "Fire_Domain"

    # Make the domain a bit taller than wide for a campfire plume
    domain.scale = (0.7, 0.7, 1.05)
    bpy.ops.object.transform_apply(location=False, rotation=False, scale=True)

    # Assign volume material
    domain.data.materials.append(volume_mat)

    # Fluid modifier: DOMAIN
    mod = domain.modifiers.new(name='Fluid', type='FLUID')
    mod.fluid_type = 'DOMAIN'
    dset = mod.domain_settings  # REQUIRED NAME

    # --- VERIFIED dset.* assignments ONLY ---
    dset.domain_type = 'GAS'
    dset.resolution_max = int(DOMAIN_RESOLUTION)

    # Noise: disabled for REPLAY preview (noise generally relies on separate bake)
    dset.use_noise = False

    """Attach Mantaflow FLOW settings to an emitter mesh."""
    mod = emitter.modifiers.new(name='Fluid', type='FLUID')
    mod.fluid_type = 'FLOW'
    fset = mod.flow_settings  # REQUIRED NAME

    fset.flow_type = 'FIRE'
    fset.flow_behavior = 'INFLOW'

    # Fuel/heat controls (simple starting values)
    fset.temperature = 1.0
    fset.density = 1.0

    fset.velocity_normal = 1.5

    scene = bpy.context.scene

    # Camera
    bpy.ops.object.camera_add(location=(2.2, -2.2, 1.55))

def setup_compositor_glow():
    """Optional: add a subtle glare to brighten flame highlights.

    try:

        nt = scene.node_tree
        if nt is None:

        nodes = nt.nodes
        links = nt.links
        nodes.clear()

        n_rl = nodes.new('CompositorNodeRLayers')
        n_rl.location = (-400, 0)

        n_glare = nodes.new('CompositorNodeGlare')
        n_glare.location = (-50, 0)
        n_glare.glare_type = 'FOG_GLOW'
        n_glare.quality = 'MEDIUM'
        n_glare.mix = 0.25
        n_glare.threshold = 0.8

        n_cc = nodes.new('CompositorNodeColorBalance')
        n_cc.location = (180, 0)
        # Warm the highlights slightly
        n_cc.lift = (1.0, 1.0, 1.0)
        n_cc.gamma = (1.05, 1.0, 0.98)
        n_cc.gain = (1.08, 1.03, 0.95)

        n_out = nodes.new('CompositorNodeComposite')
        n_out.location = (430, 0)

        links.new(n_rl.outputs['Image'], n_glare.inputs['Image'])
        links.new(n_glare.outputs['Image'], n_cc.inputs['Image'])
        links.new(n_cc.outputs['Image'], n_out.inputs['Image'])

    ensure_dir(RENDER_DIR)

    render_frames()

{"code":"import bpy
import os
import math
from mathutils import Vector

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# shakedown_fire_2iter - Mantaflow Fire (REPLAY cache)
# Blender: 5.0.1
#
# IMPORTANT CONSTRAINTS (per provided VERIFIED API SPEC):
# - Only these FluidDomainSettings attributes are assigned:
#   domain_type, resolution_max, use_noise, noise_strength, vorticity,
#   use_adaptive_timesteps, timesteps_max, use_dissolve_smoke,
#   dissolve_speed, cache_type, cache_directory, openvdb_cache_compress_type
# - Only these FluidFlowSettings attributes are assigned:
#   flow_type, flow_behavior, temperature, density,
#   use_initial_velocity, velocity_normal
# - No fluid bake operators are used (none were verified).
#   We rely on dset.cache_type='REPLAY' and render frames sequentially.
# ------------------------------------------------------------

ASSET_NAME = "shakedown_fire_2iter"

FRAME_START = 1
FRAME_END = 10

DOMAIN_RESOLUTION = 32

CACHE_DIR = f"//cache_{ASSET_NAME}"
RENDER_DIR = f"//renders_{ASSET_NAME}"


# ---------------------------
# Utilities
# ---------------------------

def ensure_dir(blender_path: str) -> str:
    abs_path = bpy.path.abspath(blender_path)
    os.makedirs(abs_path, exist_ok=True)
    return abs_path


def clear_scene():
    # Use ops for robust deletion of default scene content.
    bpy.ops.object.select_all(action='SELECT')
    bpy.ops.object.delete(use_global=False)

    # Clean orphaned datablocks for repeatability.
    for datablock in (
        bpy.data.meshes,
        bpy.data.materials,
        bpy.data.lights,
        bpy.data.cameras,
        bpy.data.images,
        bpy.data.textures,
        bpy.data.worlds,
    ):
        for block in list(datablock):
            if block.users == 0:
                datablock.remove(block)


def look_at(obj, target: Vector):
    direction = (target - obj.location).normalized()
    obj.rotation_euler = direction.to_track_quat('-Z', 'Y').to_euler()


def set_scene_settings():
    scene = bpy.context.scene
    scene.frame_start = FRAME_START
    scene.frame_end = FRAME_END

    scene.render.engine = 'CYCLES'
    scene.cycles.samples = 96
    scene.cycles.preview_samples = 32

    scene.render.resolution_x = 1280
    scene.render.resolution_y = 720
    scene.render.resolution_percentage = 100

    scene.render.image_settings.file_format = 'PNG'
    scene.render.image_settings.color_mode = 'RGBA'

    # Mildly cinematic, stable defaults.
    try:
        scene.view_settings.view_transform = 'Filmic'
        scene.view_settings.look = 'Medium High Contrast'
        scene.view_settings.exposure = 0.0
        scene.view_settings.gamma = 1.0
    except Exception:
        pass

    ensure_dir(CACHE_DIR)
    ensure_dir(RENDER_DIR)


# ---------------------------
# World
# ---------------------------

def build_world():
    world = bpy.data.worlds.new("World_Campfire")
    bpy.context.scene.world = world

    # Keep use_nodes lines (they warn about removal in Blender 6.0 but are OK in 5.0).
    world.use_nodes = True
    nt = world.node_tree
    nodes = nt.nodes
    links = nt.links
    nodes.clear()

    out = nodes.new('ShaderNodeOutputWorld')
    bg = nodes.new('ShaderNodeBackground')

    # Dark night environment so fire reads.
    bg.inputs['Color'].default_value = (0.015, 0.015, 0.02, 1.0)
    bg.inputs['Strength'].default_value = 0.3

    links.new(bg.outputs['Background'], out.inputs['Surface'])


# ---------------------------
# Materials
# ---------------------------

def mat_ground():
    mat = bpy.data.materials.new("MAT_Ground")
    mat.use_nodes = True

    nt = mat.node_tree
    nodes = nt.nodes
    links = nt.links
    nodes.clear()

    out = nodes.new('ShaderNodeOutputMaterial')
    bsdf = nodes.new('ShaderNodeBsdfPrincipled')

    bsdf.inputs['Base Color'].default_value = (0.05, 0.045, 0.04, 1.0)
    bsdf.inputs['Roughness'].default_value = 0.95
    bsdf.inputs['Specular IOR Level'].default_value = 0.08

    links.new(bsdf.outputs['BSDF'], out.inputs['Surface'])
    return mat


def mat_log():
    mat = bpy.data.materials.new("MAT_Log")
    mat.use_nodes = True

    nt = mat.node_tree
    nodes = nt.nodes
    links = nt.links
    nodes.clear()

    out = nodes.new('ShaderNodeOutputMaterial')
    bsdf = nodes.new('ShaderNodeBsdfPrincipled')

    bsdf.inputs['Base Color'].default_value = (0.07, 0.04, 0.02, 1.0)
    bsdf.inputs['Roughness'].default_value = 0.9
    bsdf.inputs['Specular IOR Level'].default_value = 0.12

    # Very subtle ember hint.
    bsdf.inputs['Emission Color'].default_value = (1.0, 0.35, 0.1, 1.0)
    bsdf.inputs['Emission Strength'].default_value = 0.04

    links.new(bsdf.outputs['BSDF'], out.inputs['Surface'])
    return mat


def mat_stone():
    mat = bpy.data.materials.new("MAT_Stone")
    mat.use_nodes = True

    nt = mat.node_tree
    nodes = nt.nodes
    links = nt.links
    nodes.clear()

    out = nodes.new('ShaderNodeOutputMaterial')
    bsdf = nodes.new('ShaderNodeBsdfPrincipled')

    bsdf.inputs['Base Color'].default_value = (0.12, 0.12, 0.13, 1.0)
    bsdf.inputs['Roughness'].default_value = 0.99
    bsdf.inputs['Specular IOR Level'].default_value = 0.03

    links.new(bsdf.outputs['BSDF'], out.inputs['Surface'])
    return mat


def mat_fire_volume():
    """Domain volume material.

    Uses Attribute nodes ('flame', 'density') which are typical Mantaflow grids.
    If a grid is missing, its attribute reads as 0 and the shader still renders.
    """

    mat = bpy.data.materials.new("MAT_FireVolume")
    mat.use_nodes = True

    nt = mat.node_tree
    nodes = nt.nodes
    links = nt.links
    nodes.clear()

    out = nodes.new('ShaderNodeOutputMaterial')

    vol = nodes.new('ShaderNodeVolumePrincipled')
    vol.location = (520, 0)

    attr_flame = nodes.new('ShaderNodeAttribute')
    attr_flame.attribute_name = 'flame'
    attr_flame.location = (-720, 180)

    attr_density = nodes.new('ShaderNodeAttribute')
    attr_density.attribute_name = 'density'
    attr_density.location = (-720, -120)

    # Flame color ramp
    ramp = nodes.new('ShaderNodeValToRGB')
    ramp.location = (-300, 240)
    cr = ramp.color_ramp
    cr.elements[0].position = 0.0
    cr.elements[0].color = (0.0, 0.0, 0.0, 1.0)
    mid1 = cr.elements.new(0.2)
    mid1.color = (0.75, 0.08, 0.02, 1.0)
    mid2 = cr.elements.new(0.55)
    mid2.color = (1.0, 0.5, 0.06, 1.0)
    cr.elements[1].position = 1.0
    cr.elements[1].color = (1.0, 0.95, 0.7, 1.0)

    flame_mult = nodes.new('ShaderNodeMath')
    flame_mult.operation = 'MULTIPLY'
    flame_mult.location = (-300, 70)
    flame_mult.inputs[1].default_value = 32.0

    dens_mult = nodes.new('ShaderNodeMath')
    dens_mult.operation = 'MULTIPLY'
    dens_mult.location = (-300, -120)
    dens_mult.inputs[1].default_value = 2.2

    # Connections
    links.new(attr_flame.outputs['Fac'], ramp.inputs['Fac'])
    links.new(attr_flame.outputs['Fac'], flame_mult.inputs[0])
    links.new(attr_density.outputs['Fac'], dens_mult.inputs[0])

    links.new(ramp.outputs['Color'], vol.inputs['Emission Color'])
    links.new(flame_mult.outputs['Value'], vol.inputs['Emission Strength'])
    links.new(dens_mult.outputs['Value'], vol.inputs['Density'])

    vol.inputs['Anisotropy'].default_value = 0.15

    links.new(vol.outputs['Volume'], out.inputs['Volume'])
    return mat


# ---------------------------
# Geometry
# ---------------------------

def build_environment(m_ground, m_log, m_stone):
    # Ground
    bpy.ops.mesh.primitive_plane_add(size=10.0, location=(0.0, 0.0, 0.0))
    ground = bpy.context.active_object
    ground.name = "Ground"
    ground.data.materials.append(m_ground)
    bpy.ops.object.shade_smooth()

    # Logs
    for i in range(3):
        angle = i * (2.0 * math.pi / 3.0) + 0.25
        x = math.cos(angle) * 0.25
        y = math.sin(angle) * 0.25

        bpy.ops.mesh.primitive_cylinder_add(vertices=24, radius=0.05, depth=0.72, location=(x, y, 0.05))
        log = bpy.context.active_object
        log.name = f"Log_{i+1:02d}"
        log.rotation_euler = (math.radians(80), 0.0, angle + math.radians(90))
        log.data.materials.append(m_log)
        bpy.ops.object.shade_smooth()

    # Stone ring
    for i in range(12):
        angle = i * (2.0 * math.pi / 12.0)
        r = 0.38 + (0.02 if i % 2 == 0 else 0.0)
        x = math.cos(angle) * r
        y = math.sin(angle) * r
        bpy.ops.mesh.primitive_ico_sphere_add(subdivisions=1, radius=0.04, location=(x, y, 0.04))
        stone = bpy.context.active_object
        stone.name = f"Stone_{i+1:02d}"
        stone.rotation_euler = (0.0, 0.0, angle)
        stone.data.materials.append(m_stone)
        bpy.ops.object.shade_smooth()


def build_emitter():
    # Small mesh emitter near the ground.
    bpy.ops.mesh.primitive_uv_sphere_add(radius=0.06, location=(0.0, 0.0, 0.06))
    emitter = bpy.context.active_object
    emitter.name = "Fire_Emitter"

    emitter.scale = (1.0, 1.0, 0.65)
    bpy.ops.object.transform_apply(location=False, rotation=False, scale=True)

    return emitter


def build_domain(volume_material):
    # Tall-ish domain around the campfire.
    bpy.ops.mesh.primitive_cube_add(size=2.0, location=(0.0, 0.0, 1.0))
    domain = bpy.context.active_object
    domain.name = "Fire_Domain"

    domain.scale = (0.7, 0.7, 1.05)
    bpy.ops.object.transform_apply(location=False, rotation=False, scale=True)

    domain.data.materials.append(volume_material)

    # Fluid modifier: DOMAIN
    mod = domain.modifiers.new(name='Fluid', type='FLUID')
    mod.fluid_type = 'DOMAIN'
    dset = mod.domain_settings  # REQUIRED name: dset

    # --- VERIFIED dset.* assignments ONLY ---
    dset.domain_type = 'GAS'
    dset.resolution_max = int(DOMAIN_RESOLUTION)

    # Keep noise OFF for preview; enabling it often expects a separate noise bake.
    dset.use_noise = False
    dset.noise_strength = 1.0

    dset.vorticity = 0.6

    dset.use_adaptive_timesteps = True
    dset.timesteps_max = 8

    # Helps keep the domain from saturating in a short test.
    dset.use_dissolve_smoke = True
    dset.dissolve_speed = 10

    # Use REPLAY to avoid unverified bake operators.
    dset.cache_type = 'REPLAY'
    dset.cache_directory = CACHE_DIR

    dset.openvdb_cache_compress_type = 'ZIP'

    return domain


def add_flow_modifier(emitter):
    mod = emitter.modifiers.new(name='Fluid', type='FLUID')
    mod.fluid_type = 'FLOW'
    fset = mod.flow_settings  # REQUIRED name: fset

    # --- VERIFIED fset.* assignments ONLY ---
    fset.flow_type = 'FIRE'
    fset.flow_behavior = 'INFLOW'

    fset.temperature = 1.0
    fset.density = 1.0

    # IMPORTANT FIX: use verified attribute 'velocity_normal'
    # (previous script used a non-existent 'velocity_factor_normal').
    fset.use_initial_velocity = True
    fset.velocity_normal = 1.5

    return emitter


# ---------------------------
# Lighting + Camera
# ---------------------------

def build_camera_and_lights():
    scene = bpy.context.scene

    bpy.ops.object.camera_add(location=(2.2, -2.2, 1.55))
    cam = bpy.context.active_object
    cam.name = "Camera"
    cam.data.lens = 45
    look_at(cam, Vector((0.0, 0.0, 0.55)))
    scene.camera = cam

    # Key light: warm and soft
    bpy.ops.object.light_add(type='AREA', location=(1.4, -1.0, 2.3))
    key = bpy.context.active_object
    key.name = "Key_Area"
    key.data.energy = 750
    key.data.color = (1.0, 0.85, 0.7)
    key.data.size = 2.0

    # Fill: cool
    bpy.ops.object.light_add(type='AREA', location=(-1.8, 1.6, 2.1))
    fill = bpy.context.active_object
    fill.name = "Fill_Area"
    fill.data.energy = 250
    fill.data.color = (0.75, 0.85, 1.0)
    fill.data.size = 2.8

    # Rim: spot
    bpy.ops.object.light_add(type='SPOT', location=(-2.3, -0.4, 2.0))
    rim = bpy.context.active_object
    rim.name = "Rim_Spot"
    rim.data.energy = 900
    rim.data.color = (1.0, 0.95, 0.9)
    rim.data.spot_size = math.radians(55)
    rim.data.spot_blend = 0.35
    look_at(rim, Vector((0.0, 0.0, 0.7)))


# ---------------------------
# Compositor (optional glow)
# ---------------------------

def setup_compositor():
    scene = bpy.context.scene
    try:
        scene.use_nodes = True
        nt = scene.node_tree
        if nt is None:
            return

        nodes = nt.nodes
        links = nt.links
        nodes.clear()

        rl = nodes.new('CompositorNodeRLayers')
        rl.location = (-420, 0)

        glare = nodes.new('CompositorNodeGlare')
        glare.location = (-80, 0)
        glare.glare_type = 'FOG_GLOW'
        glare.quality = 'MEDIUM'
        glare.mix = 0.25
        glare.threshold = 0.8

        cc = nodes.new('CompositorNodeColorBalance')
        cc.location = (200, 0)
        cc.gamma = (1.05, 1.0, 0.98)
        cc.gain = (1.08, 1.03, 0.95)

        comp = nodes.new('CompositorNodeComposite')
        comp.location = (460, 0)

        links.new(rl.outputs['Image'], glare.inputs['Image'])
        links.new(glare.outputs['Image'], cc.inputs['Image'])
        links.new(cc.outputs['Image'], comp.inputs['Image'])

    except AttributeError:
        # Compositor API may differ depending on build.
        return


# ---------------------------
# Render
# ---------------------------

def render_frames():
    scene = bpy.context.scene
    ensure_dir(RENDER_DIR)

    # REPLAY cache sim evaluates as we advance frames; keep sequential order.
    for f in range(FRAME_START, FRAME_END + 1):
        scene.frame_set(f)
        scene.render.filepath = bpy.path.abspath(os.path.join(RENDER_DIR, f"{ASSET_NAME}_{f:04d}.png"))
        bpy.ops.render.render(write_still=True)


def main():
    ensure_dir(CACHE_DIR)
    ensure_dir(RENDER_DIR)

    clear_scene()
    set_scene_settings()

    build_world()

    # Materials
    m_ground = mat_ground()
    m_log = mat_log()
    m_stone = mat_stone()
    m_vol = mat_fire_volume()

    # Geometry
    build_environment(m_ground, m_log, m_stone)

    # Mantaflow
    emitter = build_emitter()
    add_flow_modifier(emitter)

    domain = build_domain(m_vol)

    # Camera / lights / comp
    build_camera_and_lights()
    setup_compositor()

    # Ensure depsgraph is up to date after modifiers are created.
    bpy.context.view_layer.update()

    # Render
    render_frames()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

{"code":"import bpy
import os
import sys
import math
from mathutils import Vector

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# shakedown_fire_2iter - Iter2 SpecFix ErrFix
# Technique: mantaflow_fire_replay_cache
# Blender: 5.0.1
#
# CRITICAL CONSTRAINT:
#   Only assign FluidDomainSettings / FluidFlowSettings attributes that are
#   explicitly listed in the VERIFIED API SPEC.
#
# IMPORTANT:
#   No verified bpy.ops.fluid.* bake operators are used.
#   We use dset.cache_type='REPLAY' so Mantaflow evaluates as frames advance.
#
# Output handling:
#   This script honors an optional CLI argument:
#     --output_dir <path>
#   (provided by the execution wrapper), and writes rendered frames there.
# ------------------------------------------------------------

ASSET_NAME = "shakedown_fire_2iter"
FRAME_START = 1
FRAME_END = 10
DOMAIN_RESOLUTION = 32


def parse_output_dir() -> str | None:
    """Read output directory passed by the execution wrapper."""
    if "--" not in sys.argv:
        return None
    args = sys.argv[sys.argv.index("--") + 1 :]
    if "--output_dir" in args:
        i = args.index("--output_dir")
        if i + 1 < len(args):
            return args[i + 1]
    return None


OUTPUT_DIR = parse_output_dir()

# Default fallback paths when no wrapper output_dir is provided.
DEFAULT_CACHE_DIR = f"//cache_{ASSET_NAME}"
DEFAULT_RENDER_DIR = f"//renders_{ASSET_NAME}"


def ensure_dir(path_str: str) -> str:
    """Ensure directory exists. Works with both absolute paths and Blender // paths."""
    abs_path = bpy.path.abspath(path_str)
    os.makedirs(abs_path, exist_ok=True)
    return abs_path


def clear_scene():
    bpy.ops.object.select_all(action='SELECT')
    bpy.ops.object.delete(use_global=False)

    # Clean orphan blocks for repeatability
    for datablock in (
        bpy.data.meshes,
        bpy.data.materials,
        bpy.data.lights,
        bpy.data.cameras,
        bpy.data.images,
        bpy.data.textures,
        bpy.data.worlds,
    ):
        for block in list(datablock):
            if block.users == 0:
                datablock.remove(block)


def look_at(obj, target: Vector):
    direction = (target - obj.location).normalized()
    obj.rotation_euler = direction.to_track_quat('-Z', 'Y').to_euler()


def set_scene_settings():
    scene = bpy.context.scene
    scene.frame_start = FRAME_START
    scene.frame_end = FRAME_END

    scene.render.engine = 'CYCLES'
    scene.cycles.samples = 96
    scene.cycles.preview_samples = 32

    scene.render.resolution_x = 1280
    scene.render.resolution_y = 720
    scene.render.resolution_percentage = 100

    scene.render.image_settings.file_format = 'PNG'
    scene.render.image_settings.color_mode = 'RGBA'

    # Color management
    try:
        scene.view_settings.view_transform = 'Filmic'
        scene.view_settings.look = 'Medium High Contrast'
        scene.view_settings.exposure = 0.0
        scene.view_settings.gamma = 1.0
    except Exception:
        pass


def build_world():
    world = bpy.data.worlds.new("World_Campfire")
    bpy.context.scene.world = world

    # Note: use_nodes warns about Blender 6.0 removal but is OK in Blender 5.0.
    world.use_nodes = True

    nt = world.node_tree
    nodes = nt.nodes
    links = nt.links
